texts.label: R190, Portogallo 8 ff. 92r-95r, Riario to the Earl of Desmond and to Philip II, Elvas, Jan 1581
texts.summary: Riario to the Earl of Desmond, Elvas 12 January 1581: the papal fort in Ireland is reported lost; aid is being sought. A news note: the viceroy put the garrison to the sword without resistance. A memorial to Philip II on the Italian infantry (3,037 paid, about 1,000 fit), the offer of 2,000 under the Pope's name for 4 months, and a commissary to hand them to Desmond.

texts.label: R191, Portogallo 8 ff. 98r-101r, Riario to the Secretary, [Elvas], mid-Jan 1581
texts.summary: Riario to the Secretary, mid-January 1581: the second report of the Smerwick massacre; Alba writes that the 700 Italians embarked are sick, unarmed and deserting; Philip II will not send them to slaughter and sends two ships to Ireland; Riario writes to Desmond and his brother; the Duke of Sora's affairs; an extract from the Grand Duke; Anselmo to be discharged (4,000 scudi a month owed).

texts.label: R192, Portogallo 8 ff. 195-197, Riario, 4-5 Jan 1581, with a copy of 29 Nov 1580
texts.summary: Riario to the Secretary, 4-5 January 1581: Philip II thanks the Pope for the warning about the Piedmont plot (Ayamonte, the Anselmi, Huguenots of the Dauphiné) and will not let Italy be disturbed; the English enterprise, the Italian troops and the news that has cooled the ministers. With a copy of 29 November 1580: Flanders first, the Italians embarked at Lisbon offered for Ireland or sent home.

texts.label: R193, Portogallo 8 ff. 236-238, Riario to Cardinal di Como, Badajoz 2 [Oct?] 1580 and Elvas, Dec 1580
texts.summary: Riario to the Cardinal of Como, Badajoz 2 [Oct?] 1580: Idiáquez says the King cannot undertake the English enterprise until he is master of Flanders and offers the Italians for Ireland; the nuncio will not take charge of the 1,300 badly armed soldiers. Elvas, December 1580: the President is "pietra scandali" and hostile to the Roman Court.
